Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G1583; not spoken out, i.e. (by implication) unutterable:--unspeakable.
BiblicalUsage: Peter writes of joy unspeakable and full of glory for believers who have not seen Christ yet love Him. The word names a joy that cannot be spoken out, too deep for the tongue to carry.
TheologicalSignificance: A single word for unspeakable joy holds no doctrine of its own; its beauty is Peter's, that love for an unseen Christ gives a joy words cannot hold.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
